text_blocks.snippet: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) causes high blood pressure in the lung arteries. This makes the right side of the heart work much harder to pump blood.
snippet_highlighted_words: high blood pressure in the lung arteries

text_blocks.snippet: In the early stages, PAH often causes no symptoms at all. As the blood vessels in the lungs thicken and narrow, subtle signs begin during physical activity:

list.snippet: Shortness of breath (dyspnea), especially when climbing stairs or walking
Heart palpitations or a fast, pounding heartbeat

text_blocks.snippet: As the condition worsens and strains the heart, more noticeable symptoms develop: PAH Initiative

list.snippet: Swelling (edema) in the ankles, legs, or feet
Swollen abdomen due to fluid buildup
Bluish color to the lips or skin (cyanosis)

text_blocks.snippet: You can learn more about warning signs and diagnostic testing from the American Lung Association or the Mayo Clinic.
If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, tell me:

list.snippet: Who is having these symptoms (age, general health)?
How long have they been happening?
Are there any other known heart or lung conditions?
